# Patched AvaloniaEdit TextMate adapter

This is the six-file MIT-licensed adapter from AvaloniaUI/AvaloniaEdit commit `b56a35a5d4838f3c9a9adeba90dd80952f70e774`, the source of NuGet `AvaloniaEdit.TextMate` 11.4.1. DbConnect uses this source project instead of that package. The editor and grammar resources remain NuGet dependencies at the existing resolved versions; TextMateSharp now uses the pinned [source engine](../TextMateSharp/README.md) with a protected bulk line-update operation. Syntax highlighting remains enabled.

`upstream-sources.json` records URLs and hashes of the original files. `LICENSE` is upstream's MIT license. `upstream.patch` contains the complete behavioral source delta. Unchanged upstream source intentionally retains its original style and nullable conventions. Local Git attributes preserve LF source/patch endings and allow original trailing spaces and unified-diff context lines.

The patch reconciles tokenizer line entries using the document's actual line-count delta after each change. It eliminates snapshot `RemoveLines` calls, which previously allocated three whole-document line arrays even when deleting a single character. Snapshot updates reuse the existing array when the line count is unchanged and refresh authoritative ranges starting one line before the edit, including CRLF boundary effects. Actual line-count changes still resize the snapshot array. Tokenizer entries now use one bulk range update instead of repeated middle-of-list insertion/removal; unaffected entries are preserved, and the snapshot is published under the range-update lock before invalidation. Inline edits retain their existing snapshot path. The range anchor uses the earlier of the old snapshot line and the changed document line, preserving unaffected suffix entries when CRLF delimiters split or join. A binary lookup is used only for line-count changes; snapshot storage and linear suffix-offset updating remain unchanged.

Public integration APIs and grammar/theme behavior are preserved. The unused public snapshot `RemoveLines` method remains for source/API compatibility; the production editor model no longer calls it. No private reflection, runtime patching, highlighting cutoff or strong query-history cache is used.

Validation: `dotnet test DbConnect.Tests/DbConnect.Tests.csproj -c Release --filter FullyQualifiedName~TextMateMutationTests` (also run `TextMateLineRangeTests`, `TextMateBulkTokenTests` and `EditorSelectionPerformanceTests`). These tests drive real document/model changes, allocation bounds, line readers, newline boundaries, undo/redo and tokenization against a fresh model. The opt-in undo audit runs the actual query view at 64 MiB.

To refresh upstream: fetch the same six source files and license from an explicitly selected upstream commit, update the manifest, reapply/reassess the patch, then run focused tests, the full suite and both undo-consumer cadences. Remove this fork when an upstream release passes the allocation regression and mutation tests. Do not automatically overwrite the patch during dependency updates.
